Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:1.english: A person may not sit before the barber - To get a haircut.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:3.hebrew: עד שיתפלל - שמא ישכח ולא יתפלל. והא אפילו בחול נמי? והא דתני הכא — משום דדמי להא דתני גבה: לא יצא החייט במחטו ע"ש עם חשכה, שמא ישכח ויצא משתחשך:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:3.english: Until he prays - Lest he forget and not pray. Yet isn't this [the case] even on a weekday as well? And that which [the Mishnah] taught [this] here is because it is similar to that which it taught alongside it: "A tailor may not go out with his needle on Shabbat eve near nightfall, lest he forget and go out after nightfall."

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:4.english: And one may not enter - [This too applies] adjacent to minḥa.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:5.english: Not to the bathhouse, etc. - And the reason for all of them is lest it be drawn out until the time of prayer passes.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:6.english: And if they began - [Any] one of all of these.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:7.hebrew: אין מפסיקין - אלא יגמור, ואח"כ מתפלל. ובגמרא (דף י.) מפרש בדאיכא שהות לגמור קודם שיעבור הזמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:7.english: They need not stop - Rather, he finishes and afterwards prays. And in the Gemara (10a) it explains [that this applies] when there is time to finish before the time [for prayer] passes.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:8.english: One stops for the recitation of the Shema - For it is [an obligation] from the Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:9.hebrew: ואין מפסיקין לתפלה - ובגמרא (דף יא.) פריך: הא תנא ליה רישא:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:1:9.english: And one does not stop for prayer - And in the Gemara (daf 11a), it challenges: Didn't [the tanna] teach this in the first clause?

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:2:1.hebrew: מנחה גדולה - התחלת זמן תמיד של בין הערבים, מכי מתחיל להעריב, דהיינו מחצי שבע ולמעלה. דהא חצי שש וחצי שבע חמה עומדת בראש כל אדם, וקודרת כנגדה למטה, ואינה נוטה לשום צד; ומחצי ז' ולמעלה נוטה ברקיע למערב. סמוך למנחה — מהתחלת שבע:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:2:1.english: Greater minḥa - [This is] the start of the time for the daily afternoon offering, from when [the day] begins to turn toward evening, which is from the middle of the seventh [hour] and onward [i.e., six and a half hours into the day]. For [during] the [second] half of the sixth [hour] and the [first] half of the seventh [hour], the sun stands directly overhead of every person and penetrates straight downward opposite it, and does not incline to any side; and from the middle of the seventh [hour] and onward, it inclines in the sky toward the west. [And] “adjacent to minḥa” [means] from the beginning of the seventh [hour] [i.e., midday].

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:2:2.hebrew: מנחה קטנה - בט' ומחצה, שהיו רגילין שלא לאחרו יותר מכן, כדאמרי' בתמיד נשחט. סמוך לה — מתחילת י':
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:2:2.english: Lesser minḥa - [It is] at nine and a half [hours], for they were accustomed not to delay it [the daily offering] later than this, as we say in [the chapter entitled] “Tamid Nishchat.” “Adjacent to it” — [is] from the beginning of the tenth [hour].

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:3:1.hebrew: אם התחילו אין מפסיקין - בתמיה: ויעבור הזמן?! לימא תהוי תיובתא כו' — דקתני הכא: יגמרו סעודתם:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:3:1.english: If they started, they do not stop - [This is asked] in astonishment: And will the time [for prayer] pass?! “Let us say that this will be a refutation, etc.” — for it is taught here [that] they may complete their meal.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:4:1.hebrew: בן אלעשה - חתנו של רבי היה, ופזר מעות ללמוד תספורת של כ"ג [נדרי' נא.], שהיה מספר כל ראשו, ולא לגמרי, אלא מניח כל השערות קצת, כדי שיהא ראשו של זה בצד עיקרו של זה — והיינו כסום יכסמו [את ראשיהם] (יחזקאל מ״ד:כ׳) — ומימשיך טובא:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:4:1.english: Ben Elasa - He was the son-in-law of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and he spent money to learn the haircut of the High Priest [Nedarim 51a], for he would cut [the hair of] his entire head, but not completely, rather leaving all the hairs a little [long], so that the tip of this [hair] would be next to the root of that [hair] — and this is [the meaning of] “they shall only trim [their heads]” (Ezekiel 44:20) — and it is drawn out a great deal.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:4:2.hebrew: לכולא מילתא דמרחץ - לחוף ראשו, ולהשתטף בחמין ובצונן, ולהזיע:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:4:2.english: To the entire matter of the bathhouse - To wash his head, to rinse [himself] in hot and in cold [water], and to sweat.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:4:3.hebrew: בורסקי גדולה - עורות הרבה, ובתחלת תקונן:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:4:3.english: A large tannery - [Where there are] many hides, and [it is] at the beginning of their tanning.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:1.hebrew: שמא ישבר הזוג - של מספרים, ויהא צריך לחזר אחר זוג אחר:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:1.english: Lest the pair break - [A pair] of scissors, and he will need to search for another pair.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:2.hebrew: למרחץ - נמי לא תימא לכולא מילתא דמרחץ, אלא להזיע בעלמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:2.english: Into the bathhouse - Here too, do not say [that it refers] to all matters of the bathhouse, but rather [even] merely to sweat.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:3.english: [Lest] he faint - In Old French, *pasmer* [to faint].

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:4.hebrew: לעיוני בעלמא - שאין זה תחלת עשייתה, ואפ"ה לכתחלה לא יכנס לה סמוך למנחה גדולה:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:4.english: Just to examine - For this is not the beginning of its work, and even so, ab initio he may not enter it adjacent to minḥa gedola.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:5.english: Lest he see a loss in his merchandise - Lest the hides were spoiled within it [the tannery].

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:6.english: And become preoccupied - He will be distressed, and will be preoccupied with his distress, and will not pray.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:7.hebrew: וסתרו דינא - יסתרו מה שפסקו, ויחזרו בהן, וחוזר להיות תחלת הדין:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:5:7.english: And they overturn the verdict - They will overturn what they ruled, and retract, and it reverts to being the beginning of the trial.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:6:1.hebrew: מאימתי התחלת תספורת - דנימא שוב אין מפסיק, כדתנן: אם התחילו כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:6:1.english: From when is the beginning of the haircut - So that we may say [that] he no longer interrupts, as we learned in the Mishnah: "If they began, etc."

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:6:2.hebrew: מעפורת - סודר, ונותנו על ברכיו, שלא יפול השער על בגדיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:6:2.english: A wrap - A cloth, and he places it on his knees so that the hair will not fall on his clothes.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:6:3.english: From when he removes his wrap from himself - His cloak is the first [garment removed] in taking off his clothes.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:6:4.english: From when he ties between his shoulders - [He ties] his sleeves, which they call braciere [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:7:1.hebrew: הא לן והא להו - בני בבל היו חוגרין את עצמן בחוזק, וכשאוכלין צריכין להתירם; ובני ארץ ישראל לא היו נוהגין כן בהתרת חגורה קודם נטילת ידים:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:7:1.english: This is for us, and that is for them - The people of Babylonia would gird themselves tightly, and when eating they need to loosen their belts; and the people of the Land of Israel were not accustomed to do so in loosening a belt prior to washing hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:8:1.hebrew: למאן דאמר תפלת ערבית רשות - במסכת ברכות (דף כז:), מפני שהיא כנגד הקטר חלבים ואימורים, שאין מעכבין כפרתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:8:1.english: According to the one who said the evening prayer is voluntary - [This is stated] in Tractate Berakhot (daf 27b), [and it is voluntary] because it corresponds to the burning of the fats and sacrificial portions, which do not impede their atonement.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:8:2.hebrew: לא מטרחינן ליה - להפסיק, אלא יגמור ואחר כך יתפלל:
Rashi on Shabbat 9b:8:2.english: We do not impose upon him - To interrupt [his meal], but rather he may finish and pray afterwards.

Rashi on Shabbat 9b:8:3.english: And according to the one who said [it is] obligatory, etc. - [This is said] in astonishment.

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:1:1.hebrew: לא ישב אדם לפני הספר סמוך למנחה עד שיתפלל - והא דאמר בערבי פסחים (דף צפ: ושם): "ערבי שבתות וערבי ימים טובים לא יאכל עד שתחשך" — היינו אפילו התפלל לא יאכל, כדמפרש התם: "כדי שיכנס לשבת כשהוא בתאוה"; אבל לא התפלל — אפילו בשאר ימים נמי אסור, כדאמר הכא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:1:1.english: "A person may not sit before the barber adjacent to minḥa until he prays" - And that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Arvei Pesaḥim (99b and there), "[On] the eves of Shabbat and the eves of Festivals, one may not eat until nightfall" — that means even if he prayed, he may not eat, as [the Gemara] explains there: "in order that he enter Shabbat with an appetite." But if he did not pray, it is forbidden even on other days as well, as [the Mishnah] says here.

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:1:2.hebrew: ואם התחילו אין מפסיקין - אפילו התחילו באיסור, כדמוכח בסוכה (דף לח.) גבי מי שבא בדרך ואין בידו לולב נוטלו על שולחנו, ופריך: "למימרא דמפסיקין? והא תנן: אם התחילו אין מפסיקין!", ולא משני: דהכא בהתחילו בהיתר וגבי לולב התחילו באיסור, דמצפרא זמניה הוא. וה"נ משמע בגמ' דקאמר: "כיון דשרי המייניה לא מטרחינן ליה". ויתיישב נמי הא דקשה בגמרא גבי "לימא תהוי תיובתא דריב"ל":
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:1:2.english: "And if they began, they do not interrupt" - Even if they began in a prohibited manner, as is proven in Sukkah (38a) regarding [the case of] one who was traveling and did not have a lulav in his hand, [where it states that] he takes it at his table; and [the Gemara there] asks: "Is that to say that they interrupt? But haven't we learned: 'If they began, they do not interrupt'?!" And it does not answer that here [in Shabbat] it is where they began permissibly, whereas regarding the lulav they began impermissibly, since its time [of obligation] is from the morning. And so too it is implied in the Gemara [below], which states: "Once he has loosened his belt, we do not trouble him [to stop]." And that which is difficult in the Gemara regarding "Let us say that this will be a refutation of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi" will also be resolved.

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:3:1.hebrew: אין מפסיקין - ודוקא בדאיכא שהות ביום להתפלל, כדמשמע בגמרא דקאמר: "במנחה לא שכיח שכרות" — משמע דאין לו להפסיד תפלת מנחה. ובסוכה (ג"' שם) בהדיא מוקי מתני' בדאיכא שהות, דמשני אמה שהבאתי לעיל: "הא דאיכא שהות והא דליכא שהות":
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:3:1.english: "They need not stop" - And [this applies] specifically when there is time [remaining] in the day to pray, as is implied in the Gemara, which says: "With Minchah, drunkenness is uncommon" — implying that he must not forfeit the Minchah prayer. And in Sukkah (Gemara, ibid.), [the Gemara] explicitly establishes our Mishnah as [referring to a case] where there is time, as it answers regarding what I cited above: "This is where there is time, and that is where there is no time."

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:3:2.hebrew: לימא תהוי תיובתא דר' יהושע בן לוי - משמע ליה דאפילו התחיל — מפסיק, מדאמר: "אסור לטעום". וא"ת: לוקי מתניתין בהתחיל בהיתר — דאשכחן גבי הבדלה (ע"פ דף ק'.) דקאמר נמי כי האי לישנא: "אסור לאדם לטעום כלום קודם שיבדיל", ואפ"ה משמע: אם התחילו בהיתר — אין מפסיקין, דקאמר התם: "הכי אמר רב: הבדלה אינה קובעת, וה"מ דקבעי ואכלי, אבל אתחולי מעיקרא לא מתחלינן"? ויש לומר, ד"אם התחילו אין מפסיקין" משמע ליה אפילו התחילו באיסור, כדפירש במתני':
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:3:2.english: "Let us say that this will be a refutation of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi" - [The Gemara] understood that [according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi] even if one began, he must stop, since he said: "it is forbidden to taste [anything]." And if you will say: Let [the Gemara] establish our Mishnah as [referring to a case where] one began permissibly — for we find regarding Havdalah (Arvei Pesachim 100a) that it also uses this phrasing, "it is forbidden for a person to taste anything before he recites Havdalah," and even so it implies [that] if they began permissibly they do not stop, as [the Gemara] says there: "Thus said Rav: Havdalah does not establish [an obligation to stop], and this applies where they had established [their meal] and were eating, but to begin initially we do not begin"? And one can say that [the Gemara] understood "if they began, they do not stop" as meaning even if they began impermissibly, as was explained regarding our Mishnah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:4:1.hebrew: בתספורת של בן אלעשה כו' - נראה דהכי הלכתא, ושרי סעודה קטנה במנחה גדולה עד זמן תפלה; ודוקא סעודה גדולה — כגון סעודת אירוסין ונשואין וסעודת מילה — אסור, ודלא כרב אחא בר יעקב דאסר אפילו סעודה קטנה סמוך למנחה גדולה; דהלכה כלישנא קמא דסתם לן הש"ס, ורב אשי שהוא בתראה סידר את הש"ס, והלכתא כותיה לגבי רב אחא בר יעקב. ואמאי דאמר לקמן: "מאימתי התחלת דין?", אין להוכיח דמתניתין איירי בתחלת הדין דלא כרב אחא, דאיכא למימר דקאי א"אם התחילו אין מפסיקין". ומיהו, סמוך למנחה קטנה אסור אפילו סעודה קטנה, ואם התחילו — מפסיקין. ואע"ג דהש"ס, אי לאו דר' יהושע בן לוי, הוה מוקי לה בסעודה קטנה וסמוך למנחה קטנה ואם התחילו אין מפסיקין, ולא קי"ל כר' יהושע בן לוי כדאמר בפרק תפלת השחר (ברכות כח:) — מ"מ, כיון דמסיק סתם הש"ס הכי, משמע דבהא דאם התחילו מפסיקין קיימא לן כוותיה, ודוקא בהא דאמר דאסור לטעום אפילו פירות לא קיימא לן כוותיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:4:1.english: "To a haircut of ben Elasa, etc." - It appears that this is the halakhah: that a small meal is permitted at [the time of] minḥa gedola until the time of prayer, and specifically a large meal—such as an engagement feast, a wedding feast, or a circumcision feast—is forbidden; and not in accordance with Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov, who forbade even a small meal adjacent to minḥa gedola. For the halakhah is like the first version, which the Gemara stated anonymously; and Rav Ashi, who was a later [authority], arranged the Gemara, and the halakhah is like him regarding Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov. And from that which [the Gemara] says below: "From when is the beginning of judgment?", there is no proof that our Mishnah is dealing with the beginning of judgment, contrary to Rav Aḥa; for it can be said that it refers to [the clause]: "If they started, they do not stop." However, adjacent to minḥa ketana, even a small meal is forbidden, and if they started, they must stop. And even though the Gemara, were it not for [the statement of] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, would have established it [the Mishnah] as referring to a small meal and adjacent to minḥa ketana, and [that] if they started they do not stop; and we do not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShaḥar (Berakhot 28b) — nevertheless, since the anonymous Gemara concluded thus, this implies that regarding this [matter]—that if they started they must stop—we hold in accordance with him; and only regarding that which he said, that it is forbidden to taste even fruit, do we not hold in accordance with him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:7:1.hebrew: הא לן והא לאו - פי' בקונטרס: בני בבל היו חוגרים עצמם בחוזק. וכ"מ בסמוך, מדקאמר: "הני חברין בבלאי, למ"ד תפלת ערבית רשות, מכי שרא המייניה לא מטרחינן ליה". ורבי חנינא שהיה בא"י — היה אומר לתלמידיו שהיו מבבל, ורב שהיה מבבל — אומר לתלמידיו שהיו מא"י; לפי שדרכן היה להתרחק, שלא היו יכולין לעסוק כל כך בביתם. וקשה, דבפרק כיצד מברכין (ברכות דף מד.) בסופו, קאמר: רב חסדא אמר "על הארץ ועל פירותיה", ור' יוחנן אמר "על הארץ ועל הפירות", ואמר התם: "לא פליגי, הא לן והא להו". מתקיף לה רב נחמן ארב חסדא: "אינהו אכלי ואנן מברכינן?!" — ומאי פריך? לימא: רב חסדא אומר לתלמידיו שהיו מארץ ישראל! וי"ל: דקים ליה שבאותה שעה לא היו לפניו תלמידים מארץ ישראל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:7:1.english: "This is for us, and that is for them" - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: The people of Babylonia would gird themselves tightly. And so it is implied nearby, from what [Abaye] says: "These Babylonian colleagues of ours — according to the one who says that the evening prayer is voluntary, once he has loosened his belt, we do not trouble him [to stop his meal and pray]." And Rabbi Ḥanina, who was in Eretz Yisrael, was speaking to his students who were from Babylonia; and Rav, who was from Babylonia, was speaking to his students who were from Eretz Yisrael — because it was their custom to travel far [from home to study], since they could not engage [in study] as much in their home [towns]. And it is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mevarekhin (Berakhot 44a) at its end, [the Gemara] says: Rav Ḥisda said: "For the land and for its fruits," and Rabbi Yoḥanan said: "For the land and for the fruits." And [the Gemara] said there: "They do not disagree; this is for us, and that is for them." Rav Naḥman objected to Rav Ḥisda: "They eat, and we recite the blessing?!" And why did he object? Let him say that Rav Ḥisda was speaking to his students who were from Eretz Yisrael! And one can say: it was clear to him that at that time, there were no students from Eretz Yisrael before him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:8:1.hebrew: למ"ד תפלת ערבית רשות לא מטרחינן ליה - וא"ת: תיפוק ליה משום ק"ש? וי"ל: כגון שקרא ק"ש. ונראה לר"י: אפילו למאן דאמר תפלת ערבית רשות — אין לבטלה בחנם, אלא בשביל שום צורך, כמו בשרא המייניה דהכא; או אם יש שום מצוה שאינה עוברת — יעשה המצוה ולא יתפלל, אע"פ שהמצוה אינה עוברת; אבל בחנם — אין לבטלה. תדע, שהרי יעקב תקנה; ולמה יש לבטלה בחנם? ועוד, דאמרינן בפרק תפלת השחר (שם כי: ושם), שהיא כנגד הקטרת אברים, שהיא כל הלילה — דלא מעכבי כפרה, אלא מצוה; ה"נ תפלת ערבית מצוה. ואין להאריך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 9b:8:1.english: "According to the one who said the evening prayer is voluntary, we do not trouble him" - And if you will say: Let him be required [to interrupt] on account of the recitation of the Shema? And one can say: For example, where he already recited the Shema. And it appears to the Ri: Even according to the one who said that the evening prayer is voluntary, one must not omit it without reason, but rather [only] for some need, such as where he loosened his belt here; or if there is some mitzvah that will not pass [i.e., is not time-sensitive], he should perform the mitzvah and not pray, even though the mitzvah will not pass; but without reason, one must not omit it. Know [that this is so], for behold, Jacob instituted it; and why should one omit it without reason? And furthermore, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShaḥar (ibid. 26b and there), that it corresponds to the burning of the limbs [on the altar], which [is performed] all night — which do not impede atonement, yet [burning them is] a mitzvah; so too, the evening prayer is a mitzvah. And one need not elaborate [further].
